# OBS004 `entry-statement`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

An `entry` statement.

## Why

`entry` gives a procedure several entry points sharing local variables, which makes control and
data flow hard to follow. It is obsolescent since Fortran 2008. Write separate procedures that share
a module-level helper.

## Reported

```fortran
entry reset(x)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
subroutine reset(x)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS004] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS004` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `OB021` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
